# Agent Black Box
See what your AI agent actually did. Build an MIT open-source, dark-first interactive execution replay, opening immediately to a useful failure/recovery graph.

## Research and architecture
Three independently versioned Cloudflare Worker applications in apps/run-importer, apps/replay-studio, apps/receipt-publisher, each with manifest, config, build and source. HTTP JSON contracts over Worker service bindings; importer owns private receipts, publisher owns explicitly approved immutable sanitized snapshots, studio owns UI. Local development uses the same fetch handlers and durable app-separated SQLite storage. No payments, accounts provisioning or arbitrary commands.
Composer source https://github.com/loftwah/app-composer: reuse pinned upstream validateManifest, validateComposition, guardPromotion (vendor/composer). Current native stack app allowlist and compose CLI support reviewed built-ins only; implement a small documented local mount/promotion adapter, never claim native registration or cloud deployment. Cloudflare deployment requires explicit authorization and configured destinations. Source ownership through separate directories/release packages, not fabricated remote repos.
RunLedger ab0ec5d: src/record.kujo plus CLI command/test entries. No schema_version upstream; explicit runledger/1 adapter envelope. Commands manually recorded, no results assumed. changed_files untimed, tests manual. Other Kujo interfaces researched, not all implemented. Canonical blackbox.run/v1 has ordered typed events, nullable timestamps, source IDs, explicit retry relationships, evidence and gaps. Strict validation, 1 MiB and 1000 events maximum. No hidden reasoning.

## Milestones
1. Contract and importer: validate, normalize, redact secrets, preserve input order and source provenance, reject duplicates/invalid versions/retry refs, surface missing results/timestamps.
2. Studio: accessible responsive dark graph/timeline/playback and evidence inspector, no raw JSON wall, reduced motion, bounded rendering, keyboard.
3. Publisher: explicit authenticated approval with reviewed content digest, private/public separated, safe public replay URLs and revocation, no auto-publication.
4. Composer integration and genuine execution: manifests and promotion checks; isolated real task recorded with RunLedger; explicit synthetic recovery fixture; upgrade one app without losing receipts.
5. Automated unit/integration/browser tests including import to public report, mobile/keyboard, actual screenshots; independent review and fixes.
6. README, architecture/schema/security/deployment/source research, 40-second recording script, technical article/social/thread/maintainer feedback, MIT/attribution; small commits; push only to authorized existing remote; Strata consolidate.

## Security and tests
Imported text rendered as text, no HTML/Markdown interpretation, commands never executed, URLs never fetched, HTTPS links safely constrained. Server-owned private auth, same-origin writes, no browser-generated authority. Redaction heuristic with explicit residual-risk disclosure. Resource limits before JSON parse, depth and string bounds. Published records exclude private storage references. Tokens/cost/duration unknown unless evidence supports them. Test malformed/oversized inputs, version/order/duplicates/null timestamps, incomplete tools, retries/provenance/redaction, denied publication, graph/timeline/playback, independent upgrade, Composer upstream validators, responsive and accessibility. npm test, npm run test:e2e, npm run build are gates. Use actual Loop harness .loop-engineering configuration proven in current source. Record gates and blockers without claiming unexecuted checks.

# Decisions
Use app-owned storage and versioned HTTP contracts. Reuse Composer validators unchanged. Offline PackWrite manifest authored by this agent; no provider generation.

## Confirmed
Three app-owned Worker boundaries.
## Open
Public destination and remote ownership require user selection.

## Log
